Seven configured targets remain covered by `MainProp`, `NashWilliams`, `SuperNW`, `GBetterRelIff`, `Subarr`, `BqoIffGeneralShift`, and `RadoEmbedding`. The universe-generalization task is complete, and `PowerQ`, `PowerChild`, `PowerChildWellFounded`, `PowerSupport`, `PowerSupportNonempty`, `PowerPresentationEq`, `PowerPresentationEqEquivalence`, and `PowerSupportInvariant` now supply the hierarchy core. The recent removal of the two redundant equation-wrapper nodes does not reopen that task. The next missing declaration is genuinely `PowerRel`; there is no lifted order, comparison-game package, hereditary carrier, or target-covering node yet.

The present `PowerQ Q` is the right raw carrier for the route: it has disjoint atom/node constructors, arbitrary nonempty `Type u`-indexed nodes, child well-foundedness, and extensional presentation equivalence. The order may be defined on raw presentations provided it is proved invariant under `PowerPresentationEq` in both arguments. No quotient is required for the preservation proof, but no downstream argument may confuse raw equality with extensional equality. The existing `SetDomination` and `PowerWqoBadPairSequence` belong to the first-level Rado branch and do not attach to any of the three uncovered targets.

The first target must be reached through the manuscript's exact four clauses at lines 1404-1419 and the reflection argument at lines 1533-1550. Negating those clauses yields a canonical one-round Player I response from a failed pair: at a left node choose a child witnessing failure, while at a left atom stay put; every legal response on the right leaves another failed pair. Global classical choices must be functions of the compared presentations, not fresh choices indexed by the input infinite set. Iterating these choices along the shift orbit gives the copied triangular plays. Well-founded child descent proves termination, but termination alone is not enough: the package must prove that the terminal left atom for `X` depends on only finitely many values `h(X), h(Shift X), ..., h(Shift^k X)`. Together with a finite-shift/prefix lemma and local constancy of `h`, that is what proves the reflected map locally constant.

After that reflection theorem, the first covering statement is:

```text
PowerQPresBqo: [IsPreorder Q r] -> Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r).
```

For the hereditary targets, keep the carrier as the induced hereditary part of the full hierarchy. A countably branching tagged code with an erasure into `PowerQ` is a convenient witness; `HereditarilyCountable x` should mean that `x` is `PowerPresentationEq`-equivalent to an erased code. This representation must prove closure under nonempty countable families by choosing codes and reindexing the family by `Nat`; finite families can be repeated. `HerCtblRel r` is then the restriction of `PowerRel r` to the subtype.

There is one necessary refinement to the old converse task. Paper lines 1559-1564 explicitly form the singleton sequence only when the front is nontrivial. If `F = {empty}`, singleton nodes are not in `PrefixTree F`, so an unconditional `ConverseGame` statement is false or ill-typed. State the construction for `empty notin F` (or an equivalent nontriviality condition). In the eventual reverse implication, the deciding front is nontrivial because an empty deciding prefix would make the locally constant multi-sequence constant, contradicting badness and reflexivity. The recursion still needs a new extension-oriented well-founded theorem: on the prefix-tree subtype, `child` is below `parent` when `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. The existing `FrontTreeWellFounded` has the opposite argument orientation and must not drive `TildeF`.

The remaining target statements should be:

```text
BqoHerCtblWqo:   [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellQuasiOrdered (HerCtblRel r)).

BqoHerCtblWellF: [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellFounded
    (fun a b => HerCtblRel r a b and not HerCtblRel r b a)).
```

For the wqo theorem, the forward direction is `PowerQPresBqo`, the elementary `BqoImpliesWqo`, and restriction to the hereditary subtype. The reverse direction passes from a bad locally constant multi-sequence to its deciding-front bad super-sequence, proves that front nontrivial, and applies the hereditary `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded theorem, wqo gives well-foundedness of the strict part via `WellQuasiOrdered.wellFounded`. The converse is special to this hereditary carrier: from a bad sequence `a`, make the countable tail node `T n` containing `a (n+k)`. Reflexivity gives `T (n+1) <= T n`, while badness at index `n` rules out `T n <= T (n+1)`, producing a descending strict chain. Do not use a false general well-founded-implies-wqo principle.

Proceed in the task order below and claim coverage in the order `PowerQPresBqo`, `BqoHerCtblWqo`, `BqoHerCtblWellF`. Existing correspondence or substantiveness debts on unrelated covered branches are verifier work and do not justify reopening the completed universe or hierarchy-core tasks.

## Claim being audited

Seven configured targets remain covered by `MainProp`, `NashWilliams`, `SuperNW`, `GBetterRelIff`, `Subarr`, `BqoIffGeneralShift`, and `RadoEmbedding`. The uncovered set is unchanged: `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The Tablet has nevertheless advanced materially since the previous plan. The universe-generalization task is complete, and `PowerQ`, `PowerChild`, `PowerChildWellFounded`, `PowerSupport`, `PowerSupportNonempty`, `PowerPresentationEq`, `PowerPresentationEqEquivalence`, and `PowerSupportInvariant` now supply the hierarchy core. The recent removal of the two redundant equation-wrapper nodes does not reopen that task. The next missing declaration is genuinely `PowerRel`; there is no lifted order, comparison-game package, hereditary carrier, or target-covering node yet.

The present `PowerQ Q` is the right raw carrier for the route: it has disjoint atom/node constructors, arbitrary nonempty `Type u`-indexed nodes, child well-foundedness, and extensional presentation equivalence. The order may be defined on raw presentations provided it is proved invariant under `PowerPresentationEq` in both arguments. No quotient is required for the preservation proof, but no downstream argument may confuse raw equality with extensional equality. The existing `SetDomination` and `PowerWqoBadPairSequence` belong to the first-level Rado branch and do not attach to any of the three uncovered targets.

The first target must be reached through the manuscript's exact four clauses at lines 1404-1419 and the reflection argument at lines 1533-1550. Negating those clauses yields a canonical one-round Player I response from a failed pair: at a left node choose a child witnessing failure, while at a left atom stay put; every legal response on the right leaves another failed pair. Global classical choices must be functions of the compared presentations, not fresh choices indexed by the input infinite set. Iterating these choices along the shift orbit gives the copied triangular plays. Well-founded child descent proves termination, but termination alone is not enough: the package must prove that the terminal left atom for `X` depends on only finitely many values `h(X), h(Shift X), ..., h(Shift^k X)`. Together with a finite-shift/prefix lemma and local constancy of `h`, that is what proves the reflected map locally constant.

After that reflection theorem, the first covering statement is:

```text
PowerQPresBqo: [IsPreorder Q r] -> Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r).
```

For the hereditary targets, keep the carrier as the induced hereditary part of the full hierarchy. A countably branching tagged code with an erasure into `PowerQ` is a convenient witness; `HereditarilyCountable x` should mean that `x` is `PowerPresentationEq`-equivalent to an erased code. This representation must prove closure under nonempty countable families by choosing codes and reindexing the family by `Nat`; finite families can be repeated. `HerCtblRel r` is then the restriction of `PowerRel r` to the subtype.

There is one necessary refinement to the old converse task. Paper lines 1559-1564 explicitly form the singleton sequence only when the front is nontrivial. If `F = {empty}`, singleton nodes are not in `PrefixTree F`, so an unconditional `ConverseGame` statement is false or ill-typed. State the construction for `empty notin F` (or an equivalent nontriviality condition). In the eventual reverse implication, the deciding front is nontrivial because an empty deciding prefix would make the locally constant multi-sequence constant, contradicting badness and reflexivity. The recursion still needs a new extension-oriented well-founded theorem: on the prefix-tree subtype, `child` is below `parent` when `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. The existing `FrontTreeWellFounded` has the opposite argument orientation and must not drive `TildeF`.

The remaining target statements should be:

```text
BqoHerCtblWqo:   [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellQuasiOrdered (HerCtblRel r)).

BqoHerCtblWellF: [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellFounded
    (fun a b => HerCtblRel r a b and not HerCtblRel r b a)).
```

For the wqo theorem, the forward direction is `PowerQPresBqo`, the elementary `BqoImpliesWqo`, and restriction to the hereditary subtype. The reverse direction passes from a bad locally constant multi-sequence to its deciding-front bad super-sequence, proves that front nontrivial, and applies the hereditary `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded theorem, wqo gives well-foundedness of the strict part via `WellQuasiOrdered.wellFounded`. The converse is special to this hereditary carrier: from a bad sequence `a`, make the countable tail node `T n` containing `a (n+k)`. Reflexivity gives `T (n+1) <= T n`, while badness at index `n` rules out `T n <= T (n+1)`, producing a descending strict chain. Do not use a false general well-founded-implies-wqo principle.

Proceed in the task order below and claim coverage in the order `PowerQPresBqo`, `BqoHerCtblWqo`, `BqoHerCtblWellF`. Existing correspondence or substantiveness debts on unrelated covered branches are verifier work and do not justify reopening the completed universe or hierarchy-core tasks.
